preamble: Backing and rounding of [i] to [u] is rare as a regular change but occurs as a conditioned assimilation after labials, especially the rounded labial-velar glide [w], which spreads its rounding and backness to the following high vowel. In Old English, early widu 'wood' and widuwe 'widow' developed variants wudu and wuduwe; wudu became the standard form and survives as Modern English wood.

examples.note: Assimilated after w; wudu is the usual later form and the ancestor of Modern English wood.
West Saxon variant with the same rounding after w.
